subject: RFI: Air-gapped deployment & supply chain controls for Redwood Private
messages:
From: Megan Lewis <megan.lewis@veridianhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Air-gapped deployment & supply chain controls for Redwood Private

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for agreeing to review our air-gapped requirements. As part of our vendor security review for Veridian Health's edge deployment program we need detailed answers to the following within the week:

1) High-level architecture for an air-gapped on-prem deployment (hardware, network zones, jump hosts, and break-glass procedures).
2) Complete SBOM (components and versions) for the runtime and orchestration layers; if you cannot share full SBOM, a summary with provenance is acceptable.
3) Firmware and BIOS vetting policy for recommended server SKUs, and whether Redwood performs independent verification or relies on the vendor.
4) Chain of custody and secure shipment procedures if Redwood will ship preconfigured images or appliances.
5) KMS/HSM integration and whether customers can supply their own HSMs (BYOHSM).
6) Patch management cadence, signed updates, and out-of-band emergency patch process.
7) Evidence of SOC 2 / ISO controls that specifically map to private deployment operations (we will need a countersigned attestation or redacted report).

Also: do you have an installation playbook we can review, and can Redwood attend an on-site technical workshop with our infra team the week of Mar 22?

Procurement has copied me on contract timing constraints — we need to validate controls ahead of a PO.

Appreciate a point-by-point reply and any artifacts you can share.

Best,
Megan Lewis
Senior IT Security Manager
Veridian Health
megan.lewis@veridianhealth.com
From: rachel.kim@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Air-gapped deployment & supply chain controls for Redwood Private

Hi Megan —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find an initial point-by-point summary below and a set of starter artifacts attached. We can follow up with the on-site workshop and deeper evidence (including a redacted SOC 2 attestation) during the workshop or via secure transfer. Proposed workshop slots: Mar 22 or Mar 24; let me know which works.

Attachments included: redwood-airgap-capabilities.pdf, sbom-summary.csv (redacted), initial-onprem-playbook-exec-summ.pdf

Summary answers (high level):
1) Architecture: Redwood Private supports a fully air-gapped topology with a management jump host hosted in the customer DMZ, separated compute nodes inside a restricted VLAN, and optional physical HSMs in a secure rack. We recommend an out-of-band encrypted USB for initial bootstrap, signed images, and an operator-only console on a separate management NIC.

2) SBOM: Attached is a redacted SBOM summary (components + provenance). For full SBOM we can provide an NDA-protected package or bring it to the workshop.

3) Firmware/BIOS vetting: We maintain a documented supplier vetting checklist and capture vendor-signed firmware versions. We do not recompile firmware, but we run a validation step that includes signature checks, boot measurements, and a whitelist of firmware versions we approve for supported SKUs.

4) Chain of custody: We offer two options — customer-supplied images and on-site provisioning, or Redwood-prepared encrypted images shipped in tamper-evident packaging with an audited courier and chain-of-custody manifest. We log receipt and perform image signature verification prior to any install.

5) KMS/HSM: We support integration with customer-managed HSMs (BYOHSM) via PKCS#11 and KMIP. We also provide an optional Redwood-managed software-backed KMS for customers who cannot host an HSM. Keys used by the runtime are always wrapped with an HSM when available.

6) Patch mgmt: Normal cadence is monthly maintenance windows; critical patches are handled via an emergency process that includes signed, auditable packages and an out-of-band approval workflow. For air-gapped installs we provide signed delta packages and in-person or secure-transfer options for distribution.

7) Evidence: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and a signed operations attestation.

Next steps: if you confirm which artifacts you need in full (full SBOM vs. redacted; full SOC 2 vs. attestation), we'll prepare the secure transfer. I can also schedule a 60–90 minute technical workshop with Solutions + Security.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Megan Lewis <megan.lewis@veridianhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com, cjordan@veridianhealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Air-gapped deployment & supply chain controls for Redwood Private

Thanks Rachel — this is a helpful start. A few clarifications and requests before the workshop:

- For firmware vetting: can you confirm whether Redwood stores firmware hashes on your side and whether you provide an attestation that the image was tested against those hashes? We need to ensure we have measurable proof rather than procedural descriptions.
- Chain of custody: please provide a sample manifest and courier SLA.
- BYOHSM: can you confirm supported vendor list (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, etc.) and whether Redwood integrates with FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules?
- Patch mgmt: does Redwood perform routine vulnerability scanning on the images you ship? What tooling do you use and can you share scan reports redacted?
- Playbook: we asked for the on-site install playbook — ideally a step-by-step runbook (network cutover, account provisioning, key injection, smoke tests). The exec summary is fine but we need operational detail.

Also: our legal team will need a countersigned attestation that Redwood will not retain customer keys for air-gapped deployments and that any backups are covered under Veridian's encryption policy.

Can you do a second pass and include example artifacts where possible?

Thanks,
Megan

Hannah: please pull the redacted SOC 2 attestation and prepare a countersigned operations attestation template for review; include contact for PSIRT and emergency patching.

I'll coordinate the DocuSign bundle and confirm the workshop slot once we have the docs.

Thanks —
Rachel

Hi Megan —

Appended below is a consolidated response and the artifacts we can share today (redacted where required). We can deliver the full SBOM and unredacted scan reports under an NDA or bring them to the on-site workshop.

Attachments (today): redwood-airgap-capabilities.pdf, sbom-summary.csv, onprem-install-playbook-v1.pdf, attestation-soc2-redwood_signed.pdf
Secure transfer / signature: https://app.docusign.com/some/docusign-link/VER-2027-1123
Jira ticket for evidence pack: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-1182

Key points:
- Firmware hashes: we store expected firmware hashes in a secure internal repo (read-only, audited). For any shipped images we include the image manifest with the hash and provide a signed attestation that the image scanned/validated against the stored hash. Language for that attestation is included in the attached operations attestation PDF.

- Chain of custody: sample manifest is in the onprem-install-playbook-v1.pdf. We partner with vetted couriers; manifest includes tamper-evident serials and a signed receipt flow. SLA for shipping + delivery confirmation is included in the playbook appendix.

- BYOHSM: supported vendors include Thales, Utimaco, and AWS CloudHSM (KMIP/PKCS#11). We support FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules and will map the specific module IDs in the full SBOM under NDA.

- Vulnerability scanning: we run static and dynamic scans on build artifacts and perform signed image scans prior to shipping. Example redacted scan reports can be provided; tooling includes industry scanners and CVE monitoring feeds — details in the security appendix.

- Playbook: attached is a draft step-by-step runbook for on-site install, including network cutover checklists, key injection steps, smoke tests, and rollback procedures.

- Key custody: for air-gapped deployments we support BYOHSM; Redwood will not retain customer private keys when BYOHSM is used. For deployments that opt for Redwood-managed KMS we document key wrapping and access controls; the operations attestation covers retention and backup constraints.

Next actions: confirm which artifacts you want delivered under NDA vs. in-workshop. If you approve the DocuSign bundle I will have legal countersign the attestation and we can lock the workshop for Mar 22 (preferred) or Mar 24.

Regards,
